title: Pitiless Plunderer + Ashnod's Altar + Reassembling Skeleton: is the loop mana-positive?

you: Reassembling Skeleton — already sacrificed to pay the cost of Ashnod's Altar's mana ability, now in your graveyard

scenario.mana_available: {C}{C} in your mana pool from Ashnod's Altar; every land tapped

stack.note: Reassembling Skeleton died; create a Treasure token
Reassembling Skeleton died; each opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life

extras.note_for_the_resolver: Branch threat-v1 of edgar-vampires (data/decks/edgar-vampires/branches/threat-v1/cards.json) runs Pitiless Plunderer, Reassembling Skeleton and Zulaport Cutthroat; the sleeved list does not yet. It is your main phase and no opponent responds. Ashnod's Altar's ability is a mana ability and does not use the stack.
extras.assumptions: No opponent interacts; the question is whether the loop sustains itself and what each cycle nets.

scenario.question: Resolve both triggers, then: using the {C}{C} in your pool and the Treasure, can you pay {1}{B} for Reassembling Skeleton's ability, return it to the battlefield tapped, and sacrifice it to Ashnod's Altar again — and does every such cycle leave you with more mana than it started with, so it repeats indefinitely within this main phase? State the net mana and the life each opponent loses per cycle, and whether the Skeleton returning tapped matters.

steps.action: Starting position. Reassembling Skeleton has already been sacrificed to Ashnod's Altar ('Sacrifice a creature: Add {C}{C}.'). The Altar's ability is a mana ability: no target, adds mana, not loyalty. It resolved immediately, off the stack, putting {C}{C} into your pool. Skeleton died, and the trigger events of Pitiless Plunderer ('Whenever another creature you control dies, create a Treasure token') and Zulaport Cutthroat ('Whenever this creature or another creature you control dies, each opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life') both matched.
steps.effect: Pool {C}{C}. Skeleton in the graveyard. Two triggers on the stack: Plunderer at pos 0 (bottom) and Zulaport at pos 1 (top). Lands all tapped. Hand empty.

steps.effect: Each opponent loses 1 life: 40 -> 39 at each of the three seats, 3 across the pod. You gain 1 life. The scenario does not give your starting life, so only the +1 is stated. Pool still {C}{C}: mana stays in the pool until the end of the step or phase, and this is still your main phase.

steps.action: Cycle begins. You activate Reassembling Skeleton's ability ('{1}{B}: Return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped.') from the graveyard, which is the only zone it works in. While paying, you activate the Treasure's mana ability: tap and sacrifice it for {B}. Then you pay {1} with one {C} from the pool and {B} with the Treasure's black.
steps.effect: Cost {1}{B} paid in full. Pool after payment: {C}. Treasure gone. The Treasure is not a creature, so sacrificing it does not trigger Plunderer or Zulaport. The ability is on the stack. The Treasure is the ONLY source of {B} on this board (the Altar makes only {C} and every land is tapped), so each cycle depends on the previous cycle's Plunderer trigger resolving before the next activation.

steps.effect: Reassembling Skeleton returns to the battlefield TAPPED. You receive priority. Pool {C}.

steps.action: Holding priority, you activate Ashnod's Altar and sacrifice the tapped Skeleton.
steps.effect: It being tapped does not matter. The Altar's cost is only 'Sacrifice a creature' with no {T} symbol, so neither the tapped-permanent restriction on costs nor summoning sickness applies. The mana ability resolves at once: pool {C} + {C}{C} = {C}{C}{C}. Skeleton dies again, and Plunderer and Zulaport both trigger once.

steps.action: The next time you would receive priority, the game checks state-based actions and you put both triggers on the stack in any order. All players pass twice and both resolve, Zulaport and then Plunderer, or the other way round. The order does not change the result.
steps.effect: Each opponent loses 1 life (39 -> 38), so the pod loses 3, and you gain 1. One new untapped Treasure. End of cycle: pool {C}{C}{C} plus one Treasure. The cycle started with {C}{C} plus one Treasure, so you are back at the same board with exactly one extra {C}.

steps.action: Repeat. Every action in the loop is optional, because activating the Skeleton and sacrificing it are your choices. So it is not a mandatory loop that draws the game. You may name a shortcut: a number of iterations that ends at a point where you have priority.
steps.effect: After N cycles the pool holds {C} x (2+N). Opponents are each at 39-N and you have gained 1+N in total. At N = 39 (40 deaths counting the one already paid), every opponent is at 0. State-based actions then make all three lose the game together at the next check. The pool empties at the end of the main phase, so excess {C} must be spent in this phase or is lost. The loop itself is unbounded within the phase.

citations.quote: Loops that contain an optional action don’t result in a draw.
This sequence may be a non-repetitive series of choices, a loop that repeats a specified number of times
If a player has 0 or less life, that player loses the game.
Each player’s mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase, and the player is said to lose this mana.

final_state.summary: YES, the loop is mana-positive. Each cycle spends {1}{B}: one {C} from the pool plus the Treasure as {B}. It returns {C}{C} from Ashnod's Altar and a fresh Treasure from Pitiless Plunderer, for a net +{C} per cycle with the Treasure replaced. It also drains 1 from EACH opponent per cycle (3 across the pod) and gains you 1. The Skeleton returning tapped does not matter, because the Altar's cost has no {T}. The binding constraint is colour: the Treasure is the only {B} source, so every cycle must wait for Plunderer's trigger to resolve. Only {C} accumulates, and it empties at the end of the main phase. From 40/40/40, the pending Zulaport trigger plus 39 cycles take all three opponents to 0, and they lose to state-based actions.

summary_notes: All 35 quotes were checked against lookup-rule; every one is verbatim or an accurate fragment.

Rulings were read for Pitiless Plunderer (2018-01-19) and Zulaport Cutthroat (2021-03-19), which are simultaneous-death clarifications that do not apply here. Ashnod's Altar and Reassembling Skeleton have no official rulings. No step contradicts a ruling.

Tool disagreement: scenario-facts lists Pitiless Plunderer and Zulaport Cutthroat under other_permanents with creature_bodies [], because it reads the sleeved cards.json. branches/threat-v1/cards.json types both as Creature. The resolution does not depend on the body count beyond Skeleton being 'another creature'.

The resolution quotes no sibling stack figures, so the comparability check does not apply. validate-stack OK with three not-in-the-99 warnings: the line runs on branch threat-v1, not the sleeved list.

Missing-step audit is clean: SBA (704.3) at steps 3 and 7, priority after resolution (117.3b) and after mana abilities (405.6c), trigger ordering (603.3b), mana pool emptying (106.4), loop shortcut (732.2a), and mandatory-loop exclusion (104.4b) are all present.
